messages:
olivia: heads up — we're seeing an ECC correctable error surge on pool-eu-west-2-gpu starting ~11:03 UTC, per-card corrigible counts ~1.2k/hr vs baseline ~40. node labels: gpu-pool-eu-12{card-3,card-7,card-9} hit hardest. alert: https://alerts.redwood.ai/alert/12345 :warning:

samir: grabbing telemetry now, will tail dmesg and nv-hostengine logs. can we hold off on full replacements? prefer to try soft-drain + kernel retry tuning first. :thinking:

infra-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-281. severity=medium. related metric: gpu.ecc.correctable.rate. current window=5m. triggered_by=olivia.

jenny: quick numbers — 3 cards exceed the per-card burst threshold (burst_threshold=500/min). Xid counts show recent increases in Xid 31 and Xid 43. attaching sample log snippet:
```
[11:04:12] gpu0: ECC corrected error on physical addr 0x7f9a3b... count=254
[11:04:13] gpu0: Xid 31 send error to host
```

oncall-sre: if this is transient noisy card we want minimal disruption to clusters. propose: 1) soft-drain affected cards for 10m 2) bump kernel RT retry to reduce retries causing Xid noise 3) monitor for 15m, escalate to full drain+replace if counts keep > threshold. :+1:

samir: agree. to soft-drain we can run: `rbacctl node-drain gpu-pool-eu-12 --cards 3,7,9 --mode soft --grace 600 --reason "ECC spike"` — this will evict new jobs but keep KV cache. also will add a fallback route to route small requests to pool-eu-west-3.

olivia: do it. start with two nodes as canary (gpu-pool-eu-12-node17, node19) not whole pool. notify latency/product teams about potential perf bump. jenny, samir — keep me posted on Xid progression.

jenny: canary started at 11:07 UTC. commands run:``nctl drain --node node17 --cards 3,7 --soft --grace 600``. telemetry link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/gpu-health?var-pool=eu-west-2&from=now-30m

infra-bot: Action log — soft-drain executed on node17,node19 by samir at 11:07:22 UTC. autolink: INC-2026-281 -> runbook/soft-drain-2026.md

oncall-sre: monitoring window open. if corrected error rate drops below 100/hr per card within 10m, we keep alive and revert kernel tweak. if not, escalate to reserved-capacity mitigation and schedule full replacement.

samir: quick note — I applied a local driver param tweak to increase hardware retry count from 8->12 on node17 (non-persistent) to see if Xid 31 disappears. will revert if no effect.

jenny: 11:14 update — corrected error rate halved on node17, but node19 still climbing. both nodes still over burst threshold globally. taking node19 off routing for a second canary (soft offline) to isolate.

olivia: good. plan B if node19 stays noisy: mark card as quarantined and schedule a replacement during next maintenance window. for now we avoid immediate swap to keep capacity.

oncall-sre: decision summary (pasted to incident): 1) Canary soft-drain on node17+19 at 11:07 2) Kernel retry bump on node17 only (transient test) 3) Monitor 15m — if sustained > 500/min for any card -> automatic escalation to hard-drain + replace 4) Route low-latency traffic to eu-west-3 during remediation window 5) Postmortem if replacement required.

samir: adding a small automation hook: if `gpu.ecc.correctable.rate` > 800/min for 5m on >2 cards in pool -> `autodrain` will soft-drain affected nodes and notify oncall. will dry-run for 48h before enabling. command stub:
```
autodrain --pool eu-west-2 --threshold 800 --duration 300 --mode soft --dry-run=true
```

jenny: +1 to dry-run. please also add a slack message to #eng-infra with a short summary when automation triggers so triage can confirm.

olivia: agreed. for post-incident action items: - tune burst_threshold per region (eu-west-2 seems lower SNR) - add runbook snippet for canary soft-drain - add escalation to Dedicated capacity fallback if we risk SLOs - schedule replacement for any card hitting >5k corrected errors in 24h.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-281 updated: status=monitoring. assignees=samir,jenny. followup tasks created in taskboard: TB-9876.

oncall-sre: closing thread for now — will reopen if automation dry-run triggers or node19 continues to worsen. :mag_right:
